entries.note: REJECTED against its own pre-registered criteria: below the 95% bar by a wide margin (6%), and the per-year rows are carried by 2020-21. The video's result is the 2020-21 bull market plus overfitting to BTC. Side observation, deliberately NOT acted on: the random long-green-candle baseline itself printed +0.148R net. That is a number found while testing something else, on a bull-heavy window, and chasing it would be the forking-path mistake this test was built to avoid; if ever pursued it needs its own pre-registration and a disjoint window.

entries.question: How much of the ledger's R rests on inferring, from a 15m bar's colour, which of its high and low traded first when the bar reaches both a take-profit and the stop?
entries.evidence: Built 2026-10-28 as /whatif intrabar (wolf/whatif.compare_intrabar), after reviewing rsalianto/tradoor, whose grader books such a bar as the stop. The live tracker infers the order (intrabar_tp_first=True since it was introduced) and that inference had never been measured. Paired: the same resolved trades replayed twice on 15m bars, inferred vs stop-first, both through the replay (never replay against the stored ledger), each cut at the signal's own timeout because the older whatif replays grade bars the live position never saw. (Written at build time that stop-first is a floor; it is not. Taking the stop side first also skips the breakeven re-check on a bar that fills TP1, so on those bars stop-first books more than the inferred order. The card was corrected on 2026-10-30.) READ 2026-10-30 (/whatif intrabar, first read after the code was finally deployed): scored 63 of 290 resolved signals (the rest beyond the ~10-day 15m reach); inferred and stop-first identical on every trade, changed 0 of 63, tied 63, diff +0.0000R, 6 open at the cut. Per strategy all zero (MOMENTUM 16, SCALP 21, TRAP 16, PREDUMP 8, PREPUMP 1, SWING 1). Both read +0.181R gross over these 63.
entries.note: Criteria written before any read. |stop_first - inferred| < 0.02R/trade: the inference is immaterial; close as INCONCLUSIVE-not-material and stop asking. Gap <= -0.05R/trade with padj < 0.05: the ledger's gross is optimistic by up to that much; quote it beside every meanR given to the owner and on /paper's net line, and do NOT flip the live default to stop-first on this alone (both are assumptions; flipping would also break comparability with every card since 09-08). Anything between: report the bound, re-read once on a disjoint sample. Also print and read the tie count — trades that never straddle a bar must score identically, and a low tie rate on trades with wide bars is expected, not a fault. OUTCOME: below the pre-registered 0.02R threshold (measured 0.0000R), so closed as not material. One bound to carry: zero changes in 63 puts the straddling rate under ~4.8% at 95% (rule of three), and a straddle moves a trade by at most ~1.5R, so the worst case is ~0.07R/trade. That is a bound, not an estimate, and it is the reason this is INCONCLUSIVE rather than settled at zero. One re-read on a disjoint sample is enough; do not re-open otherwise.

entries.question: How much of each trade's R is BTC moving under the position rather than anything the detector read, and did the bot sit on BTC's side or against it?
entries.evidence: Built 2026-11-02 as /beta (wolf/beta.py), after reviewing tradermonty/claude-trading-skills, whose residual-edge-analyzer asks whether a strategy's returns survive a predeclared baseline. No card had asked it: 09-28, when every strategy stopped out together, read as six failures when it was plausibly one market move. Not yet read. PARTIAL READ 2026-11-02 (/beta, whole log requested): only 231 of 497 trades priced, over 13 days; 266 fell outside the BTC bars because the bot's client answered from a venue serving 300 hourly bars (~12.5 days). So this is the most recent ~13 days, a window and not the whole log. Fixed the same day: bars now come from Binance's public data host first (1000 bars, ~41 days) and the card prints the bar source and reach. Figures, for the record and NOT the pre-registered read: slope b +1.06 (clustered se 0.11, t +9.23, nom +6.21, df 12), R^2 0.14; meanR +0.002 = from BTC +0.047 (x-bar +0.045) + rest -0.045, rest net -0.132; WITH 118 trades +0.245 vs AGAINST 113 -0.251. ETH agrees: b +0.85, from ETH +0.042, rest -0.040. Groups (pooled b): LONG -0.151 (from BTC -0.013, rest -0.139), SHORT +0.177 (from BTC +0.115, rest +0.062); PREDUMP +0.482 (from BTC +0.160, rest +0.322) the largest rest; all padj >= 0.457. On criterion (1) the window sits at the line (|0.047| vs 0.05, t well past 2); read the full log before deciding which side. READ 2026-11-02 (pre-registered, whole log, after the reach fix): 497 of 497 trades over 26 days, bars binance 1000 = 41.6 days, outside history 0, clipped 0. Slope b +1.29 (clustered se 0.15, t +8.54, nom +10.20, df 25), R^2 0.17. meanR -0.000 = from BTC +0.055 (x-bar +0.043) + rest -0.055; rest net -0.142. WITH 251 trades +0.337 vs AGAINST 246 -0.344. ETH: b +0.90 t +9.08 R^2 0.19, from ETH +0.061, rest -0.061 (agrees in sign of b and x-bar). Groups on pooled b, none padj<0.05: LONG -0.159 (from BTC +0.021, rest -0.180, padj 0.106), SHORT +0.179 (+0.093, rest +0.086, 0.434), MOMENTUM -0.090 (+0.016, -0.106, 0.308), PREDUMP +0.316 (+0.133, +0.183, 0.308), PREPUMP n=14 -0.449 (+0.014, -0.463, 0.106), SCALP +0.010 (+0.076, -0.066, 0.532), SWING n=22 -0.050 (+0.104, -0.154, 0.532), TRAP -0.034 (+0.012, -0.046, 0.532). OUTCOME on criterion (1): |from BTC| 0.055 >= 0.05 with t >= 2, ETH agreeing: MATERIAL. The ledger's flat gross is BTC's drift (+0.055R/trade) cancelling a negative remainder (-0.055 gross, -0.142 net) - removing the market makes the bot worse, not better.
entries.note: Choices fixed before any read. Baseline BTCUSDT 1h (1000 bars, ~41 days, past the capped log), ETHUSDT the one sensitivity check; no other baseline may be added after seeing a result. x = BTC % move from activation to exit, interpolated inside the hour, signed toward the trade, divided by the trade's stop distance (own R), clipped at +-3R. y = gross R; net = gross rest less the group's mean assumed round trip. OLS y = a + b*x with standard errors clustered by UTC exit day (df = days - 1). Groups LONG, SHORT and each strategy use the pooled b; each group's rest tested for zero, BH-FDR across groups. A positive b is EXPECTED by construction (alts follow BTC; a long gains when its coin rises), so b>0 alone settles nothing. READ the whole log with /beta. (1) x-bar and 'from BTC' = b*x-bar: if |b*x-bar| >= 0.05R per trade with b's clustered t >= 2, BTC's drift is a material part of meanR; report the share, and read every later per-strategy sign flip beside BTC's move in the same window. (2) If |b*x-bar| < 0.05R: the bot is close to BTC-neutral on average and the flat-gross/negative-net reading stands unchanged; close INCONCLUSIVE-not-material. (3) R^2 is how much of trade-to-trade noise is market; report it, act on nothing. (4) ETH must agree in sign of b and of x-bar; disagreement reads as fragile, not as either answer. (5) 'rest' (the intercept) is in-sample and NEVER alpha; a positive group rest is a pattern for the next disjoint read, not a finding. Under rule 1 no outcome here changes a gate, a filter or a strategy: a market-regime filter would be a strategy change, and this card does not test one. Re-read once on a disjoint log (~4 weeks), no more. CAVEAT ON THE OUTCOME, written at the read: 'from BTC' is b times x-bar, and x-bar rests on a WITH rate of 251/497 = 50.5% - a coin flip. The bot did not choose BTC's side; BTC happened to drift with its net book (mostly shorts while BTC fell, see SHORT from BTC +0.093). So read +0.055 as tailwind the period supplied, not as a skill that will recur; a disjoint log can hand back zero or a headwind. Consequences: quote the rest (-0.055 gross / -0.142 net) beside every pooled meanR given to the owner, and read every per-strategy sign flip beside its 'from BTC' column. No gate, filter or strategy changes (rule 1). Re-read once on a disjoint log (~4 weeks), no more.

entries.question: Does an Elliott Wave wave-2 -> wave-3 entry, applied by fixed rules without hindsight, pick better entry moments than random entries with the same stop, target and time cap?
entries.evidence: Built 2026-11-06 as /ewtest (wolf/ewtest.py), offline only, after the owner (who counts waves by hand) asked whether Elliott Wave could join the bot. Not yet read. Calibration on synthetic random walks before any real read: 80 null runs (40 seeds x long/short) gave a uniform-looking spread of 'beats' (mean 51.9%), and 3 of 80 cleared 97.5% against a nominal 2.5% - so the bar is close to its stated size, slightly generous. PARTIAL READ 2026-11-06 (/ewtest BTC, one coin only, not the pre-registered basket): BTCUSDT 4h since 2020-10-28. LONG n=49 wr 20% gross +0.244 net +0.127, target 6 / stop 39 / timeout 4, 1R 2.08%; random same-geometry median -0.065, p97.5 +0.788, beats 73%. SHORT n=44 wr 16% gross -0.331 net -0.459, target 3 / stop 37 / timeout 4; random median -0.211, p97.5 +0.500, beats 22%. Both sides n<100 -> INCONCLUSIVE by the criteria. Years swing widely (2023 +14.9R, 2026 -15.2R): a 1.618 x W1 target is a ~4-6R target with a ~20% hit rate, so the per-trade spread is wide and the random p97.5 sits far above the median. The full ten-coin /ewtest is the read. READ 2026-11-06 (pre-registered, plain /ewtest, ten coins 4h since 2020-10-28): LONG n=543 wr 22% gross +0.034 net -0.037 total -20.2R, target 37 / stop 419 / timeout 87, 1R 3.45%; random same coin/side/stop/target median +0.024, p97.5 +0.217, beats 24%. SHORT n=490 wr 22% gross -0.036 net -0.115 total -56.5R, target 27 / stop 368 / timeout 95, 1R 3.01%; random median -0.066, p97.5 +0.145, beats 28%. Both sides n >= 100 and well under the 97.5% bar -> REJECTED on both: the wave-2 entry times the market no better than random entries with identical geometry (slightly worse, in fact). Per coin net: LINK +0.295 and LTC +0.217 the only clear positives, BNB -0.277, ADA -0.280, ETH -0.274 the worst - a spread to expect from ten coins under a null, and the best two are a max over ten, not a lead. Years: 2023 +41.9R, 2024 -56.6R, 2026 -42.8R. Scope of the rejection: this one rigid rule set (4h, 3xATR zigzag, 50-61.8% zone, 1.618 target, 60-bar cap). It does not test discretionary counts with other context; it does say the wave-2 setup alone is not an entry signal. Do not re-open by retuning the zone, the target or the timeframe on this data - that is searching for the rule that fits.
entries.note: Rules fixed before any read, not to be tuned after: 4h bars, the /bbtest basket (10 majors, ~6 years from Binance's data host). Swings from a causal zigzag at 3 x ATR(14), each pivot usable only from the bar that confirmed it. Wave 1 = the last confirmed swing; wave 2 must retrace into 50-61.8% (deeper, a retake of wave 1's end, or 30 bars without a trigger kills it); entry on the next open after the first close beyond the previous bar's extreme once the zone was reached; stop at the wave-2 extreme; target wave 2 + 1.618 x wave 1; out at the close after 60 bars; a bar touching both is the stop; costs charged on each trade's own stop. Long and short are separate tests. BASELINE: for each trade, random entries on the same coin and side with the same stop %, target multiple and time cap (only the moment differs), 300 draws. SUCCESS for a side: n >= 100, net mean > 0, and beats >= 97.5% of random draws (5% split across two sides). FAIL: beats < 97.5% -> REJECTED for that side (the count does not time entries better than chance; any profit is drift or geometry). n < 100 -> INCONCLUSIVE. Even a pass is one backtest on one parameter set: it earns a pre-registered forward paper read, not a place on the live signal path (rule 1).

entries.question: Is a liquidity-sweep trade (TRAP or SCALP) better when it is taken in the London/New York hours than in the Asian and late hours, as the AMD/Power-of-3 reading of SMC says?
entries.evidence: Built 2026-11-08 as the sess: rows on /diag (wolf/diagnose._session_label), after the owner brought in a manual SMC trader's method: 5m sweeps taken in the London/NY 'manipulation' phase, CHoCH confirmation, OB retest, fixed 2R. The bot's TRAP and SCALP take the same sweep-and-reclaim at any hour and wait for no retest, so only the session part of the method is testable on existing data. The creation time of every logged signal is already recorded, so the split applies to the whole capped log (~25 days, ~270 sweep trades) the first time it is read. Not yet read; no one has seen this split. READ 1 2026-11-10 (/diag 600, window 10-16 13:28 -> 11-10 13:28 UTC, @ 1230684): TRAP+SCALP n=246. ASIA n=70 +0.104 gross / +0.028 net (fee+spread 0.076R); LONDON n=38 +0.089 / +0.014; NEWYORK n=109 +0.014 / -0.063; LATE n=29 -0.076 / -0.141; all padj 1.000. Named contrast sess:LDN+NY-ASIA+LATE gap -0.018R, se 0.338, t -0.05, df 30, eff 38, padj 1.000 (n 147 v 99). By the pre-registered rule (REJECTED if read 1 gap <= 0) the question is closed: London/New York sweeps were no better than Asian and late ones. ASIA printing the highest row is the max over four and is not a lead. This closes the session part of the manual SMC method as tested on the bot's sweeps; the CHoCH confirmation and OB-retest entry were never tested here.
entries.note: Fixed before any read and not to be moved: TRAP and SCALP only; sessions by the UTC hour of signal creation, ASIA 00-07, LONDON 07-13, NEWYORK 13-21, LATE 21-24. ONE named contrast: mean R of LONDON+NEWYORK minus mean R of ASIA+LATE, overlap-discounted, in the card's BH-FDR family (sess:LDN+NY-ASIA+LATE). The four session rows are descriptive; the best single session is a max over four and is never read as the finding. READ 1: /diag 600 now (whole capped log). READ 2: /diag 600 again on a disjoint log (~4 weeks later). SUPPORTED only if the gap is positive with padj < 0.05 on read 1 AND positive again on read 2, and the active-hours rows are positive net of their measured fee+spread. REJECTED if read 1 gap <= 0 or read 2 reverses sign. Anything else INCONCLUSIVE. Even SUPPORTED is a level finding across hours, not a filter: a session gate would be a strategy change under rule 1 and needs its own forward read. This tests session context only, not the CHoCH confirmation or the OB-retest entry the method also uses.

entries.question: Do the two textbook Ichimoku entries (Tenkan/Kijun cross, cloud breakout), applied by fixed rules, pick better entry moments on the crypto basket than random entries with the same stop, target, time cap and UTC hour?
entries.evidence: Built 2026-11-13 as /ichitest (wolf/ichitest.py), offline only, after the owner sent a @thequantbuilder video: Ichimoku 9/26/52 on Nasdaq and gold M15, cloud breakout -289.6R and TK cross -549.9R, 1,000 random versions (same direction, same hour) all lost, one variant beat 97.1% of random runs with a 50.2R drawdown, and the version that looked best before 2024 made -6R after it. Not yet read. Calibration on synthetic random walks before any real read: 60 null runs (15 seeds x 2 rules x 2 sides) gave mean 'beats' 45.9% and 1 of 60 above 98.75% against a nominal 1.25% - the bar is close to its stated size. FIRST READ 2026-11-15 (plain /ichitest, ten coins 4h since 2020-11-06, per-trade baseline as registered): TK CROSS LONG n=1663 net +0.038 (before 2024 +0.089 / 2024+ -0.014), random median -0.045, beats 99% -> fails on the 2024+ half. TK CROSS SHORT n=1728 net +0.069 (before +0.022 / 2024+ +0.118), random median -0.027, p98.75 +0.035, beats 100% -> PASSES as registered. CLOUD BREAKOUT LONG n=1525 net -0.017 beats 79%; SHORT n=1548 net -0.019 beats 57% -> both fail. FAULT FOUND IN THE BASELINE BEFORE ACTING ON THE PASS: the per-trade baseline draws every random entry independently, but the rule's trades cluster in time because the ten coins move together, so the baseline's spread is far narrower than the rule's own and 'beats 99%' is not 1-in-100. The random-walk calibration could not show this because its walks were independent. Re-calibrated on baskets of ten random walks sharing a common factor (rho 0.8, no edge by construction), 128 null runs: the per-trade baseline put 14 of 128 (11%) in the outer 1.25% tails against 2.5% nominal, about four times too many. Fixed: the decisive baseline now moves the whole set of trades, all coins together, by one random whole number of days (shift_baseline). This keeps the clustering, each coin's spacing, each trade's geometry and its UTC hour. On 64 of the same correlated null runs it put 1 in the tails (1.6% against 2.5%). The per-trade figure stays on the card as 'naive', for the gap, not read. DECISION RULE FOR THE RE-READ, written before it: the same criteria (n >= 100, net > 0, beats >= 98.75% and both halves > 0) are applied with the shift baseline, and that read decides this entry. The pass above is not counted. The same per-trade flaw exists in /ewtest and /bbtest, but it only narrows the null, so their rejections (beats 24-28% and 6%) stand. DECISIVE RE-READ 2026-11-16 (plain /ichitest, shift baseline, since 2020-11-07): TK CROSS SHORT n=1729 wr 40% gross +0.117 net +0.072 total +124.0R, 1R 4.86%; before 2024 n=888 net +0.025, 2024+ n=841 net +0.121; shift median -0.021, p98.75 +0.070 -> beats 99% -> PASSES the pre-registered bar. TK CROSS LONG n=1665 net +0.039, before +0.091 / 2024+ -0.015, beats 98% -> fails (2024+ half negative, and just under the bar). CLOUD BREAKOUT LONG net -0.018 beats 76%, SHORT net -0.015 beats 59% -> REJECTED both sides. Naive per-trade figures for the gap: 99 / 100 / 78 / 61% - the correction moved TK SHORT's p98.75 from +0.035 to +0.070, i.e. the null doubled in width, and the rule still cleared it. How to hold the pass: (1) it sits just over the line (99 vs 98.75, with 300 draws); (2) the earlier half is thin (+0.025) and most of the total is 2024+; (3) across the offline tests run so far (/bbtest 1 side, /ewtest 2, /ichitest 4) the chance that at least one passes by luck is roughly one in ten; (4) both TK sides beat ~98-99% of the shifted null, which is what crypto time-series momentum would look like, and that consistency is the strongest thing in its favour; (5) funding on a ten-day short is not modelled. Per the pre-registration, a pass earns a forward paper read and never the live path. Arithmetic for that read: ~0.8 TK shorts a day across ten coins at sd ~1.3R, so confirming +0.07R needs on the order of a thousand trades (years); a forward read can catch a rule that is badly broken out of sample, not confirm this one. Offered to the owner, not built.
entries.note: Rules fixed before any read, not to be tuned after: 4h bars, the /bbtest basket (10 majors, ~6 years from Binance's data host). Ichimoku 9/26/52, the cloud at bar i is the one computed at i-26. TK cross: Tenkan closes above Kijun after being at or below on the previous bar (mirror for short). Cloud breakout: close above the cloud top after closing at or under it (mirror). Entry next bar's open; stop 2 x ATR(14) at the signal bar; target 2R; out at the close after 60 bars; stop first on a straddling bar; one position per rule per coin. The video does not state its exits, so these are a stated choice. Baseline per trade: same coin, side, stop %, 2R target, 60-bar cap, entry drawn from bars at the same UTC hour; 300 draws. Four tests (2 rules x 2 sides), so a side PASSES only with n >= 100, net > 0, beats >= 98.75% of the baseline AND net > 0 both before 2024 and from 2024 on (the video's own cut, fixed in advance). n < 100 is INCONCLUSIVE; anything else is REJECTED for that rule and side. The pre-registered read is the plain /ichitest (ten coins); a one-coin run is not the read. Even a pass earns a forward paper read, never the live path (rule 1). Do not re-open a rejection by trying other periods, exits or timeframes on this data. Outcome 2026-11-16: TK SHORT passed offline; TK LONG and both cloud breakouts rejected. Status stays OPEN until a forward read is agreed or declined.

entries.question: Does either of two momentum candidates for a replacement strategy - (A) a BTC-regime trend breakout in both directions with a trailing stop, (B) a weekly market-neutral relative-momentum book - beat a random baseline that keeps its dependence structure, net of cost, on the ten-coin 4h basket?
entries.evidence: Built 2026-11-22 as /trendtest (wolf/trendtest.py), offline only, after the owner decided to replace the live strategy (flat gross, negative net over two months) instead of tuning it. They allowed shorts ('asal nemu titiknya yg pas', since shorting a top that keeps rising had hurt them) and asked for coins that move differently from BTC. The candidates draw only on this project's own lessons: costs eat ~0.07-0.09R per trade (so trade less and wider), most of the ledger was BTC beta (so follow the market on purpose, or cancel it), liquid books did better (so stay on majors), and the only external rule to clear an offline bar was a momentum rule. Not yet read. Calibration before any real read, on baskets of ten random walks sharing a common factor (rho 0.7, no edge by construction, zero cost), 60 null runs each: A's shift baseline put 1 of 60 above 97.5% (1.7%), B's random-book baseline 3 of 60 (5%, within binomial noise of 2.5%; the baseline is a permutation of the same weeks, so exact in expectation). READ 2026-11-22 (plain /trendtest, ten coins 4h since 2020-11-13, 20bps, pre-registered): A TREND n=2842 wr 36% gross +0.131 net +0.080 total +227.4R, 1R 4.5%; LONG n=1611 net +0.071, SHORT n=1231 net +0.092; before 2024 n=1418 net +0.135, 2024+ n=1424 net +0.026; shift baseline median -0.019, p97.5 +0.098 -> beats 95% -> fails the 97.5% bar -> REJECTED. Per coin net: 8 of 10 positive (LINK -0.07, LTC -0.01 ... BNB +0.19). B MOMENTUM 309 weeks, mean +0.140%/wk, win 49%, total +18.1%, max DD 53.2%, worst week -21.06%; before 2024 +0.683%/wk, 2024+ -0.435%/wk; random-book median -0.190%, p97.5 +0.360% -> beats 85% -> REJECTED (also fails the 2024+ half). How to hold A's miss: it is the most consistent offline result this project has produced (net positive on both sides, both halves and 8 of 10 coins, gross +0.131 against a cost of only ~0.05R at a 4.5% stop), and 95% is a one-sided p of about 0.05 for a single test. But the bar was 97.5% because two candidates were tested, the 2024+ half is thin (+0.026), and A shares its data and its momentum idea with the TK-cross pass, so the two are not independent confirmations. The rejection stands as registered. Do not re-open by trying other regime lengths, breakout lengths, stop or trail multiples on this data. The only legitimate next look at A is forward, on bars that did not exist when this was read: unchanged rules, pre-registered kill criterion, paper only, and at ~1.3 trades a day it can catch a rule that breaks, not confirm +0.08R (that needs on the order of 1,000+ trades). Offered to the owner, not built.
entries.note: Rules fixed before any read, not to be tuned after. 4h bars, the /bbtest basket (10 majors, ~6 years, Binance data host). A: regime = BTC 4h close vs its 300-bar mean (UP/DOWN); longs only in UP, shorts only in DOWN; entry when a 4h close goes beyond the previous 20 bars' high (long) or low (short), filled at the next open; initial stop 2xATR(14); trailing stop at 3xATR from the best price, never loosened, tested before it moves; no fixed target; out at the close after 90 bars; stop first on a straddling bar; gaps fill at the open; one position per coin. B: every Monday 00:00 UTC rank by 28-day return, long top 3 / short bottom 3, equal weight, half the book each side, exit at next Monday's open, a full 20bps round trip charged on the whole book every week. Baselines: A, the whole trade set moved by one random number of whole days (keeps cross-coin clustering, side, stop and trail distance, UTC hour); B, the same weeks with a random 3 long / 3 short. Two tests, so each PASSES only with n >= 100 (A trades / B weeks), net > 0, beats >= 97.5% of its baseline, and net > 0 both before 2024 and from 2024 on. Otherwise REJECTED (or INCONCLUSIVE if n is short). Funding is not modelled; it is a caveat on any pass, not a reason to re-run. A pass earns a forward paper run as a new era, not real money. Do not re-open a rejection by trying other lookbacks, breakout lengths, stop multiples or leg counts on this data - that is searching for the rule that fits.

entries.question: Does the trend-breakout rule (candidate A of trend-and-relative-momentum, rejected offline at 95% against a 97.5% bar) keep a non-negative net expectancy on bars that did not exist when it was read?
entries.evidence: Built 2026-11-22 as wolf/v2.py ('gas paper A'). Runs candidate A unchanged and forward, on its own paper ledger (store key v2_paper, start 1000, 1% risk per trade, 20bps charged on each trade's own stop), posting entries and exits to the High-Conviction topic labelled 'paper - belum lolos tes'. It calls wolf.trendtest's own functions (btc_regime, breakout_side, walk_trail), so the forward run and the backtest cannot drift. Not yet read.
entries.note: Rules are the offline A rules, unchanged: BTC 4h close vs 300-bar mean for regime, 20-bar closing breakout with the regime, fill at the next bar's open, 2xATR initial stop, 3xATR trail tested before it moves, 90-bar cap, one position per coin, ten-coin basket. Only the newest closed bar is read each pass, so a signal missed while the bot was down is skipped, never filled late. KILL RULE, fixed before any trade: once 300 trades have closed, a mean net R below zero stops new entries for good (open positions still resolve). No promotion rule exists: at ~1.3 trades a day, 300 trades (~8 months) can catch a rule that broke out of sample but cannot confirm +0.08R, which needs on the order of 1,000+ trades. Nothing here is a real-money signal. Do not change the rule while it runs; a changed rule is a new entry with a new start date.

entries.question: Does averaging down with a half-gap exit on the added lot (the Copilot atlas's ADD + recovery, slide 05) add expectancy to the same entries, or only win rate?
entries.evidence: Built 2026-11-22 as /addtest (wolf/addtest.py), offline only, after the owner shared the 'KORO / COPILOT math atlas' of another live bot (70% win rate at payoff ~1, +61% over 3 days on $14 equity) and asked to learn from it. Paired on /trendtest A's own entries, so the market move cancels. Not yet read. Calibration on 8 correlated null baskets (no edge, 20bps): the gap ADD - plain was -0.03 to -0.06R a trade (t -3.4 to -6.1), win rate up 1-2 points, worst 1% from about -1.05R to -1.60R, the added lot alone winning ~55% at about -0.10R each. So on data with no edge the instrument shows averaging down as a cost (one extra round trip, plus the conservative bar order that never fills the target on the add bar), and a real-data gap near -0.05R reads as 'no different from no edge'. A first version closed both units at the half-gap target; it was corrected before any read, because the atlas closes the added lot alone. READ 2026-11-22 (plain /addtest @ 57fb3d1, ten coins 4h since 2020-11-13, 20bps per unit, pre-registered): 2842 paired trades over 991 entry days; ADD fired on 1503 (53%), half-gap target hit 1039. PLAIN win 36%, net +0.079R, worst 1% -1.12R, worst -1.18R. ADD win 38%, net +0.092R, worst 1% -1.67R, worst -1.86R. Gap ADD - plain +0.0133R/trade, se 0.0073 clustered by day, t +1.82 -> under the t >= 2 bar -> REJECTED as registered. The added lot alone won 69% at +0.025R each. The prediction written before the read held on all three counts: win rate up (36 -> 38%), mean not significantly up, worst 1% about 50% deeper. One thing to hold, and not to act on: the null calibration put the gap at -0.03 to -0.06R and the lot at about -0.10R, so on real 4h crypto the added lot did about +0.1R better than on no-edge data. That is a sign of short-horizon mean reversion inside these breakout trades. It is post hoc, it sits under the bar, and it buys about 0.013R a trade for half again the tail, so it is not a lever. Do not retune ADD_AT or the target to chase it on this data.
entries.note: Rules fixed before any read: entries are exactly /trendtest A's (4h, ten coins, ~6y, BTC regime, 20-bar breakout, 2xATR risk R, 3xATR trail, 90-bar cap). The first unit is the plain trade, unchanged. If price moves 0.5R against the entry, before the first unit's stop and while its trail sits below that level, one lot is added at that level (or at the open on a gap). That lot alone exits at the half-gap target (entry + fill)/2, never on the add bar, or at the stop the first unit has in force (stop first on a straddling bar), or at the 90-bar cap. Each unit pays 20bps on its own round trip. Results are in R of the first unit, clustered by entry day. PASS (ADD improves expectancy) only if the paired gap is > 0 with t >= 2; otherwise REJECTED. Prediction written before the read: win rate up, mean not up, worst 1% worse. Even a pass changes nothing live: v2 runs its rule unchanged, and averaging down would be a new forward entry. Do not retune ADD_AT or the target on this data.

entries.question: On v2's forward trades, do coins whose recent 4h returns continue (lag-1 autocorrelation > 0 and 24h variance ratio > 1, the Copilot atlas's universe test) do better than the rest?
entries.evidence: Built 2026-11-22: every v2 entry records rho1 and VR(q=6) over the coin's last 180 4h log returns and a label PERSIST / NOT (None when the history is short or flat). It is a label only and never filters, so v2's rule is unchanged. Shown on the /v2 card, the entry message and the dashboard. Not yet read.
entries.note: Read once, at v2's 300-trade kill-rule point (or when v2 stops): the gap PERSIST - NOT in net R, with the standard error clustered by entry day. It counts only if the gap is > 0 with t >= 2 and PERSIST is net positive; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE. Expect it to be underpowered: about 150 trades a side cannot resolve much under ~0.2R. Edges (rho1 > 0, VR > 1, W = 180, q = 6) are fixed and are not to be tuned.

entries.question: Do daily high/low zones known at 00:00 UTC (the @chebito87 'predicts the daily high and low' indicator, in a naive form) contain the day's extremes as often as claimed, and does fading them earn more than fading zones placed on random days?
entries.evidence: Built 2026-11-22 as /zonetest (wolf/zonetest.py), offline only. The owner sent a TikTok claiming a '90% winrate over 4 years'. Its chart is coverage (the share of days whose extreme fell inside the zone), not a trade win rate, and its last chart claims ~88% of days within +/-0.25 ADR20 of a forecast made before the day. The formula is unpublished, so a naive zone stands in: open + median(last 60 days of (high - open)/ADR20), and the mirror for the low, with half-width 0.25 ADR20. Calibration on correlated random-walk baskets (13,000 4h bars, ten coins): naive coverage high 42% / low 46% / both 26%; within +/-0.25 ADR 42-46%. The fade there won 58% of trades at about -0.21R net, because the coarse 4h bar order is charged against it, and the random-day baseline is charged the same way. Over 20 null runs, 0 cleared the 97.5% bar (max 92%). Not yet read. READ 2026-11-22 (plain /zonetest @ de82f72, ten coins 4h since 2020-11-14, pre-registered): COVERAGE 21,190 coin-days: high inside the zone 55%, low 53%, both 31%; within +/-0.10/0.25/0.50 ADR of the centre: high 23/55/83%, low 21/53/83%. So a zone built from only the open and ADR20 lands about 55% at +/-0.25 ADR, against the video's ~88%. Real data beats the random walk (42-46%) because daily ranges cluster, but it is nowhere near 88%. FADE n=33,876, won 66%, gross -0.004R, net -0.078R, 1R 2.96%; SHORT -0.078, LONG -0.078; before 2024 -0.064, 2024+ -0.092; random-day zones median -0.080, p97.5 -0.077 -> beats 89% -> REJECTED (net negative in both halves as well). The fade won two trades in three and still lost: it collects many small returns to the open and pays for the days that run through the zone, then the cost. Naive day-zones carry no forecast that the fade can trade.
entries.note: Rules fixed before any read: 4h bars from the /bbtest basket (10 majors, ~6y), UTC days of six complete bars. ADR20 is the mean high-low range of the prior 20 days. Zone centre: open + median of the prior 60 days' (high-open)/ADR20, each day's ratio on its own causal ADR20 (mirror for the low). Half-width 0.25 ADR20. COVERAGE is descriptive: high/low/both inside the zone, plus the share within +/-0.10/0.25/0.50 ADR; it is read against the video's ~85-90% and ~88%. FADE: first touch of the near edge (short at the high zone's bottom, long at the low zone's top); stop at the far edge (risk 0.5 ADR20); target the day's open; out at the day's last 4h close; stop first on a straddling bar; the target never fills on the entry bar; gaps fill at the open; 20bps a round trip. Baseline: the same days and geometry with each day's centre offsets from a random other day of the same coin, 300 draws. PASS only with n >= 100, net > 0, beats >= 97.5%, and net > 0 both before 2024 and from 2024 on; otherwise REJECTED. The absolute net is pessimistic by construction (4h order), so read the gap to the baseline, not the level. Do not retune the half-width, the centre window or the target on this data.

entries.question: Does the Threads screenshot's plan, reduced to fixed rules (trade only with the D1/H4 trend, enter when an H1 bar sweeps the last swing against the trend and closes back, stop beyond the sweep, target the last opposite H1 swing), beat the same trades moved to random days, net of cost?
entries.evidence: Built 2026-11-22 as /sweeptest (wolf/sweeptest.py), offline only. The owner sent a screenshot from someone else's Threads post: an MT5 terminal with an AI (Opus) sidebar planning a BTC short ('Plan #45': sell zone 60,900-61,080 after an H1 sweep of the high, SL 62,050, TP 55,250 at the H1/2-year low, void on an H4 close above 64,018). That plan was judged sound in structure (with-trend, defined stop, ~1:5), but a single chart says nothing about edge, and an LLM's plans cannot be backtested as such. This is the mechanical core. The data is ~2.7 years of 1h bars on the ten-coin basket, paged from Binance's data host.  Calibration on correlated 1h random-walk baskets (24,000 bars, ten coins, 20bps): 0 of 30 null runs cleared the 97.5% bar (max 93%). On noise the rule won ~30% at a median target of ~2.6R, with 1R ~0.9%, so cost alone runs ~0.2R a trade at H1 stop widths. READ 2026-11-25 (plain /sweeptest, ten coins 1h since 2024-02-29, pre-registered): n=2613, won 29%, gross -0.009R, net -0.314R, total -821.5R, median 1R 0.82%, median target 2.56R; exits target 739 / stop 1865 / cap 9. LONG n=969 -0.342, SHORT n=1644 -0.298; first half (to 2025-10-19) -0.287, second half -0.342. Same trades on random days: median -0.286, p97.5 -0.128 -> beats 27% -> REJECTED (also net < 0 in both halves). All ten coins net negative (ETH -0.59 worst, AVAX -0.08 best). Gross is zero to two decimals, so the trend filter plus the sweep carries no timing at all, and the real figures sit almost exactly on the null calibration (win ~30%, target ~2.6R, 1R ~0.9%): on this rule set the market reads as a random walk. The -0.31R net is cost: at H1 stop widths 20bps is ~0.3R a trade. The screenshot's 1:5 shape is what the geometry gives, not evidence of an edge.
entries.note: Rules fixed before any read. Trend: the last complete daily close below EMA50 and EMA200 and the last complete 4h close below EMA50 allows shorts only; the mirror allows longs only; anything else, no trade (D1/H4 built from the 1h bars). Swings: H1 fractals, a high above 3 bars either side, usable from the confirming bar (3 later). Signal: an H1 bar trades through the last confirmed swing high (low for longs) and closes back inside; each swing is used once. Entry at the next open. Stop at the sweep extreme +/- 0.25xATR(14,1h). Target: the last confirmed opposite swing, skipped if under 1R. 120-bar (5-day) cap; stop first on a straddling bar; gaps fill at the open; one position per coin; 20bps per round trip on each trade's own stop. Baseline: the whole trade set moved by one random number of whole days (side, stop %, target multiple, cap and hour kept), 300 draws. PASS only with n >= 100, net > 0, beats >= 97.5%, and net > 0 in both halves split at the median trade date; otherwise REJECTED. The H4 'void above 64,018' layer is not modelled (the stop covers it). Do not retune pivot width, stop buffer, the EMA set or the 1R floor on this data.

entries.question: Does v2's rule (/trendtest candidate A: BTC-regime 20-bar breakout, 2xATR stop, 3xATR trail, 90-bar cap), moved bar for bar to 1h or 15m for scalping, beat the same trades moved to random days, net of cost?
entries.evidence: Built 2026-11-25 as /trendtest 1h and /trendtest 15m (wolf/lowtftest.py), offline only. The owner asked whether v2 could run on a lower timeframe 'buat scalping' as a v3, after being told v2 may not be promoted by lowering its 97.5% bar to the 95% it reached. The live v2 (4h, forward paper) is untouched; a v3 paper run is built only if this passes. PREDICTION written before any read: cost in R scales with 1/ATR and ATR shrinks roughly with the square root of the bar length, so A's ~0.05R a trade at 4h (gross +0.131, net +0.080) becomes ~0.10R at 1h and ~0.20R at 15m, while nothing in this project's lower-timeframe record shows gross growing to pay it (old SCALP/TRAP on 15m flat gross; /sweeptest on 1h gross -0.009R, net -0.314R; /addtest hinted at short-horizon mean reversion inside breakouts). Expected: 15m fails; 1h most likely fails. Calibration on baskets of six correlated random walks (rho 0.7, 6000 bars, no edge, zero cost, 100 draws): 1h 0 of 30 null runs over 97.5% (mean beats 43%, max 96%); 15m 0 of 30 (mean 40%, max 90%). A full-size synthetic 15m run (ten coins x 35,000 bars, 200 draws) took ~6s here. READ 1h 2026-11-25 (plain /trendtest 1h, ten coins since 2024-02-29, pre-registered): n=5358, win 34%, gross +0.093R, cost 0.120R, net -0.028R, total -148.2R, median 1R 1.95%; LONG -0.063, SHORT +0.008; first half (to 2025-07-22) -0.022, second half -0.033; shift baseline median -0.089, p97.5 +0.003 -> beats 92% -> 1h REJECTED (net < 0, both halves < 0, under the bar). Per coin: six of ten between -0.02 and +0.03, BTC/BNB/LTC about -0.10. The prediction held on both counts: cost came in at 0.12R (predicted ~0.10R), and gross did not grow to pay it. What it adds: gross is still positive (+0.093 against +0.131 at 4h) and the timing beats random days by ~0.06R, so the breakout carries some momentum on 1h too; it is simply smaller than the 1h cost.
